package_info.package_manager: N/A (core infrastructure, not a package manager)
package_info.package_versions: All versions prior to PR 81056 / issue #1711 fix
package_info.why_malicious: A race condition vulnerability in Kubernetes allowed nodes with duplicate hostnames to overwrite each other's state in etcd, leading to cluster instability and potential denial of service. While not a traditional 'malicious package', this logic flaw could be exploited by an attacker with node-joining privileges to disrupt or crash the cluster by intentionally creating duplicate node identities.

execution_context.trigger: When a node joins the cluster (cluster registration event)
required_permissions: network access to communicate with the master node
ability to set the node's hostname or use --hostname-override

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
etcd key: /registry/minions/HOSTNAME
# HOSTNAME is not enforced to be unique
# Each node update overwrites the same key if hostnames are duplicated
malicious_snippets.code_language: Go (Kubernetes core logic, conceptual etcd key usage)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a node joins the cluster, the registration logic writes the node's state to etcd under the key /registry/minions/HOSTNAME, without enforcing uniqueness of HOSTNAME, resulting in updates from multiple nodes with the same hostname overwriting each other, which causes cluster state corruption and instability.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Allowing multiple nodes to register with the same hostname enables a race condition that can be intentionally triggered to disrupt cluster operations, as each node's state update overwrites the other's in etcd.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Cluster management systems are expected to enforce unique identifiers for each node to maintain integrity; failing to enforce hostname uniqueness allows malicious actors to undermine cluster state consistency.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: A legitimate use case is a single node rejoining after a reboot, updating its own state, but not multiple active nodes with the same hostname simultaneously.
key_indicators: No uniqueness check on node hostname during join
Frequent overwrites of the same etcd key (/registry/minions/HOSTNAME) from different nodes
Cluster instability and high CPU load on master node after node join events
Multiple nodes reporting identical hostnames in cluster state

execution_context.trigger: When a node is started with the --hostname-override flag set to an existing node's hostname

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During node startup, if the kubelet is launched with --hostname-override set to a hostname already present in the cluster, the node registers under the same etcd key as the existing node, causing both nodes to overwrite each other's state and resulting in cluster instability.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The --hostname-override flag can be abused to deliberately create duplicate node identities, exploiting the vulnerability to cause state corruption and service disruption.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: The --hostname-override flag is intended for legitimate renaming or custom node identification, not for duplicating an existing node's identity in the cluster.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: In cloud environments, --hostname-override is used to set a custom node name for a single node, but not to intentionally duplicate another node's name.
key_indicators: Use of --hostname-override with a value matching an existing node's hostname
Multiple nodes reporting the same hostname in cluster state
Kubelet logs showing repeated registration attempts with duplicate hostnames

attack_chain.action: Attacker provisions a new node and sets its hostname (or uses --hostname-override) to match an existing node in the cluster.
attack_chain.leads_to: Node joins cluster with a duplicate identity, creating a conflict in the cluster state.

attack_chain.action: Both nodes periodically update their state in etcd under the same key (/registry/minions/HOSTNAME), causing a race condition as each update overwrites the other's state.
attack_chain.leads_to: Cluster state becomes unstable; master node experiences high CPU load and inconsistent node information.

attack_chain.action: Cluster instability escalates, potentially leading to denial of service or crash of the master node due to resource exhaustion and corrupted cluster state.
attack_chain.leads_to: Cluster crash or severe disruption, resulting in loss of availability and control.

behavioral_signatures: Multiple nodes reporting the same hostname in cluster state
Frequent overwrites of the same etcd key (/registry/minions/HOSTNAME) from different node IPs
Unusual spike in master node CPU usage following node join events
Kubelet logs showing repeated registration attempts with duplicate hostnames
file_indicators: Duplicate entries or frequent updates in etcd for /registry/minions/HOSTNAME
Kubelet logs containing --hostname-override usage with values matching existing nodes
network_indicators: Multiple nodes with the same hostname communicating with the master node from different IP addresses
Repeated registration requests to the Kubernetes API server from different IPs using the same node name
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor etcd for frequent updates to the same /registry/minions/HOSTNAME key originating from different node IPs. Alert if multiple nodes report the same hostname in the cluster state or if kubelet processes are started with --hostname-override set to an existing node's name. Investigate spikes in master node CPU usage following node join events, and review kubelet and API server logs for evidence of duplicate node registrations.
